cross_product_finding: This page contains an explicit backward-compatibility carve-out that sits oddly on a Capella-only page: 'For compatibility with legacy versions of Couchbase Server, a keyspace reference may comprise the bucket name only, when referring to the default collection in the default scope within a bucket.' Capella is continuously deployed with no discrete version numbers (per the registry), so a clause conditioned on 'legacy versions of Couchbase Server' is either (a) boilerplate inherited from a shared server/cloud content source describing behavior that predates Capella entirely, carried over without adaptation, or (b) evidence that Capella's query engine genuinely inherits version-sensitive parsing behavior from the underlying Couchbase Server codebase it runs on. Either reading matters for the ontology: this is exactly the kind of version-shaped fact the registry says to flag here rather than force onto `version:server-6.5`/`version:server-7.0`, since those concepts describe server/ editions' own release history, not a compatibility mode inherited by Capella.
